title: Our Lady of Guadalupe 2026: Traditions and Sending Money to Mexico
summary: Learn about Our Lady of Guadalupe Day on December 12, 2026, traditions in Mexico, and tips for sending money from the US during the holiday season.
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Our Lady of Guadalupe Day is celebrated every year on December 12. In 2026, it falls on a Saturday. The celebration honors the Virgin Mary as Our Lady of Guadalupe, a central figure in Catholic devotion and Mexican cultural identity. If you’re sending money to Mexico around this date, check your transfer’s delivery estimate and confirm your recipient’s access to the funds, including pickup-location hours.*


**A phone call to your mother in Guadalajara. A voice note from your cousin describing the candles lit outside the parish. A photo of your grandmother’s altar, decorated with roses in anticipation of December 12. For many people in the United States with family in Mexico, these small moments carry a December celebration across the distance.**


**This article has two goals. First, it explains what Our Lady of Guadalupe Day means and how people observe it. Second, it offers practical guidance if supporting loved ones financially is part of your December plans. Not every family marks the day the same way, and sending money isn’t a requirement of the holiday. But if you’re planning a transfer around this time, a little preparation goes a long way.**


## What is Our Lady of Guadalupe Day?


Our Lady of Guadalupe Day commemorates the Virgin Mary under the title Our Lady of Guadalupe, a figure central to Catholic devotion in Mexico and across Latin America.


According to Catholic tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to Juan Diego, an Indigenous man, at the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City in 1531. The Vatican’s own account of[the story of Juan Diego and Our Lady of Guadalupe](http://vatican.va/) describes these apparitions as the foundation of the devotion that followed.


As the story goes, roses bloomed out of season on the hillside, and an image of the Virgin appeared on Juan Diego’s tilma, or cloak. That image is now housed at the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe in Mexico City, one of the most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.


For many Mexican Catholics, Our Lady of Guadalupe holds deep religious and cultural significance. That said, not everyone in Mexico shares the same beliefs or participates in the same way. Some families attend Mass and make pilgrimages; others mark the day more quietly, or not at all.


## When is Our Lady of Guadalupe Day in 2026?


Here’s a quick reference for the date:


**Detail** **Information**


Date December 12, 2026


Day Saturday


Spanish name Día de la Virgen de Guadalupe


When observances may begin The evening of December 11


Many celebrations start the night before, with observances continuing into the early hours of December 12. Specific event schedules vary by parish and region, so if you’re looking for a program in a particular city, check local listings closer to the date.


### Is December 12 a public holiday in Mexico?


Our Lady of Guadalupe Day is not among Mexico’s nationwide mandatory rest days.[Mexico’s mandatory rest days](http://gob.mx/) are set out under Article 74 of the Federal Labor Law, and December 12 isn’t on that list.


However, December 12 does appear on Mexico’s 2026 banking holiday calendar. That distinction matters: a day can be a scheduled bank holiday without being a general public holiday. Individual institutions and locations may also operate under permitted exceptions, so it’s worth checking specific opening hours rather than assuming a blanket closure.


## How is Our Lady of Guadalupe Day celebrated?


Celebrations of Our Lady of Guadalupe Day vary by region, parish, and family, but a few traditions are widely recognized.


### Pilgrimages and visits to the Basilica


Pilgrims travel to the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe in Mexico City, and many local churches hold their own observances. Some pilgrims walk long distances or travel overnight to arrive by December 12.


### Las Mañanitas, Mass, and floral offerings


A common tradition is singing Las Mañanitas, a traditional birthday song, to the Virgin in the early hours of December 12. Religious services, floral offerings, music, and dance are also part of how[Our Lady of Guadalupe celebrations](http://visitmexico.com/) unfold in churches and public squares across Mexico. Roses, which recall the story of Juan Diego’s tilma, are a especially meaningful offering.


### Family and community traditions


Beyond church observances, some families gather for meals, attend parish events together, or simply spend time with loved ones. Because traditions differ by household and region, there’s no single “right” way to mark the day.


## How December 12 connects with the wider holiday season


Our Lady of Guadalupe Day arrives at the start of Mexico’s busiest season of celebration. Shortly after, Las Posadas begin.[Las Posadas, from December 16 to 24](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/las-posadas/) , are traditional processions re-enacting the search for lodging in Bethlehem, followed closely by Christmas and New Year celebrations.


For families who split time between the US and Mexico, this stretch of December can bring added expenses: a shared family meal, travel to see relatives, contributions toward a gathering, or everyday household costs that come with hosting guests. These are simply examples of how support might show up during the season, not assumptions about how any specific family spends the money they receive.


The core idea is straightforward: December celebrations may add to the support a family already shares with loved ones throughout the year.


## What should you know before sending money to Mexico around December 12?


If you’re planning to send money around this time, a few practical checks can help your transfer go smoothly.


### Plan around when your loved one needs the money


Start by asking your recipient when they’ll actually need the funds. Review the estimated delivery time before you confirm your transfer, and build in some room in case additional verification or processing is needed. There’s no universal “send by” date that works for everyone — it depends on your recipient’s plans and the delivery method you choose.


### Check bank and cash pickup hours


December 12 is a scheduled banking holiday in Mexico, and in 2026 it falls on a Saturday. That combination means it’s worth confirming hours at your recipient’s specific bank branch or cash pickup location rather than assuming standard weekday hours apply.


It’s also important to distinguish between funds arriving in an account and your recipient actually being able to collect or withdraw the cash. A transfer can complete on schedule, but if the pickup location is closed, your recipient may need to wait. Not every digital transfer stops, and not every cash pickup location closes — but checking in advance removes the guesswork.


### Choose a delivery method your recipient can access

Availability of each option can vary depending on the specific transfer and recipient, so confirm what’s offered before you send.


### Review the fee, exchange rate, and pesos delivered


Before confirming a transfer, review the fee, the exchange rate, and the amount your recipient will actually receive in Mexican pesos. Looking at all three together gives you a clearer picture of what your loved one can plan around. Exchange rates shift day to day, so there’s no reliable way to predict a “best day” to send — reviewing the details at the time of your transfer is the most dependable approach.


### Double-check recipient details


Before you confirm, double-check your recipient’s name and any other details required for your chosen delivery method. A small error in these details can delay a transfer, so it’s worth the extra minute to review.

### A practical scenario: Helping with a December family meal


Imagine a reader in the US who wants to contribute to a family meal in Mexico on December 12. Their relative prefers cash pickup. Before sending, the reader confirms the location’s Saturday hours, reviews the transfer estimate, and coordinates with their relative on when the money can actually be collected.


The takeaway is simple: plan around when your recipient can use the money, not just when you send it.


## Frequently asked questions


### What does Our Lady of Guadalupe Day celebrate?


Our Lady of Guadalupe Day commemorates the Virgin Mary’s apparitions to Juan Diego at Tepeyac in 1531, according to Catholic tradition. It’s a significant date in Catholic devotion and Mexican cultural identity.


### What day is Our Lady of Guadalupe in 2026?


Our Lady of Guadalupe Day falls on Saturday, December 12, 2026.


### Are banks open in Mexico on December 12?


December 12 is listed on Mexico’s 2026 banking holiday calendar, though individual institutions may operate under permitted exceptions. Check with the specific bank branch for exact hours.


### Can I send money to Mexico on Our Lady of Guadalupe Day?


You can start a transfer to Mexico on December 12. However, starting a transfer is different from your recipient being able to access the funds — bank and cash pickup hours may be affected by the holiday, so it’s worth confirming availability at your recipient’s specific location.


### When should I send money for December 12?


There’s no universal deadline. Base your timing on your transfer’s delivery estimate and when your recipient will be able to access the funds.


### Is sending money part of the holiday tradition?


No. Sending support is a personal choice some families make during the holiday season, not a religious requirement of Our Lady of Guadalupe Day.


## Staying connected this December


**However you and your loved ones mark December 12, staying connected matters more than any single transaction. If you do plan to send support this season, a quick check of delivery estimates and your recipient’s access to funds can help make sure your contribution arrives when it’s needed most.**
